subtitle: Five exercises on the text

review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: Flowers make a sweet liquid called nectar.
A bee drinks nectar with its short tongue.
The bee carries the nectar in its honey stomach.
Nectar has very little water in it.
Bees store honey to eat when flowers are hard to find.
What is the sweet liquid that flowers make?
items.why: “Flowers make a sweet liquid called nectar.”

items.q: Where does the bee carry the nectar?
items.why: “The bee carries it in a special part of its body called a honey stomach.”

items.q: What do the bees add to change the nectar?
items.why: “The bees add special substances called enzymes that help change the nectar.”

items.q: Why do the bees fan their wings?
options: To move air through the hive
items.why: “They fan their wings to move air through the hive.”

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: Bees drink nectar from flowers and carry it back to the hive in their honey stomach. In the hive, they add enzymes and fan their wings until the water evaporates. The nectar becomes thick honey, and the bees store it in the honeycomb.
It is a special part of a bee's body. The bee carries nectar in it. It is different from the stomach it uses to digest its own food.

items.q: How do bees take the water out of the nectar?
items.model: They put the nectar into honeycomb cells and fan their wings to move air through the hive. Slowly, the water evaporates.

items.q: What do the bees do when the honey is ready?
items.model: They cover the full honeycomb cells with a thin layer of wax. This keeps the honey safe.

items.q: Do you like honey? What do you eat it with?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the steps in the order of the text.
items: A bee drinks nectar from a flower
The bee carries the nectar back to the hive
The bee passes the nectar to another bee
The bees fan their wings and the water evaporates
The bees cover the honeycomb with wax
